60-70 opencast pits on the S. slope of Rosinj and Devetak. No ore found, so probably prospection pits. The scale and number of the pits in a difficult location suggests Roman workings, contemporary with the exploitation of the alluvial deposits, and in a search for primary deposits, (For the hydraulic works, see Zlatno Guvno)

A copper mining district with also extraction of silver, iron, and perhaps gold. Two bronze tablets were found here detailing the laws and regulations as well as the imperial administration's role in managing the town, granting leases, and overseeing the mining works.

Two banks of debris, 50 m wide and 10 m high, running for c. 1 km; also 31 opencast pits about 3–5 m diameter. Von Foullon 1893 description seems to indicate that this is opencast mining. Bordeaux 1904, 117, says there was an aqueduct from the Suhodol spring.

A Byzantine-period gold mining site surveyed by archaeologists in detail. 216 buildings have been identified housing an estimated labour force of 1,000.  Now heavily destroyed and damaged by modern mining.
